title: Judgment Supersession
abstract: This document records an approved and implemented architecture ruling: institutional history is append-only, and a committee decision remains permanently bound to the exact judgment that existed when that decision was recorded § Ruling . It was ruled by the architect in response to a verified defect in which re-running an analysis overwrote a judgment record in place, leaving a ledger entry pointing at a digest nothing on disk matched § Decision . The ruling selects supersession over the alternatives of archiving and freezing, and the source records the resulting data model, invariants, tests, and costs § Options put to the architect, § Implementation, § Invariants, and where they are defended, § Consequences .

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.html: This document records an approved and implemented architecture ruling: institutional history is append-only, and a committee decision remains permanently bound to the exact judgment that existed when that decision was recorded (§ Ruling). It was ruled by the architect in response to a verified defect in which re-running an analysis overwrote a judgment record in place, leaving a ledger entry pointing at a digest nothing on disk matched (§ Decision). The ruling selects supersession over the alternatives of archiving and freezing, and the source records the resulting data model, invariants, tests, and costs (§ Options put to the architect, § Implementation, § Invariants, and where they are defended, § Consequences).

sections.heading: Research Question
sections.html: The source document does not pose a research question; it is an architecture decision record. The question put to the architect was what a system should do when a case is re-analysed after a committee decision has already been recorded against a prior judgment — specifically, how to stop re-analysis from destroying the resolvability of decisions already taken (§ Decision, § Options put to the architect). The source frames the stakes in its own terms: the failure "does not produce a wrong answer — it destroys the ability to defend a right one, which is the entire reason the product exists" (§ Decision).

sections.heading: Finding
sections.html:
The defect

A committee decision cites the record digest of the judgment it was taken against. Before this change, re-running an analysis overwrote that record in place. The ledger entry then pointed at a digest nothing on disk matched, and the decision silently became undefendable (§ Decision).

The source states that this was verified rather than suspected, and records the verifying output (§ Decision):

decision cites digest : 1f8b7bfeed57e1b4
on disk after re-run  : 344d3b6d8840491d
DECISION VERIFIABLE   : False

The source classes this as "the most severe class of failure the product can have" (§ Decision).

The options and the ruling

Three options were put to the architect (§ Options put to the architect):

OptionWhat it does
ArchiveCopy the old record aside before overwriting, so decided judgments stay resolvable.
FreezeOnce a case is decided, refuse further analysis until the decision is explicitly reopened.
SupersedeA new analysis creates a new judgment. Previous decisions keep referencing the judgment they were made against. Nothing is overwritten and nothing is locked.

The ruling was Supersede, stated by the architect (§ Ruling):

A committee decision must always remain permanently bound to the exact judgment that existed when that decision was recorded. Re-analysis must never invalidate historical decisions. Do not freeze cases. Do not overwrite history. Institutional history is append-only.

The source records the reasoning for the two rejections. Freezing was rejected outright: a case that cannot be re-analysed after a decision is a case an institution cannot keep working on, and deferral is a first-class outcome in this product. Archiving was rejected because it makes the current record primary and history a side effect; supersession makes every judgment equally real and equally permanent (§ Ruling).

What was implemented

The source records the following implementation (§ Implementation):

  • JudgmentRecord on the case carries judgment_id, record_digest, recorded_on, and superseded_by. It is append-only; a new analysis marks the previous record superseded and appends its own.
  • Artifacts moved from reports/workspace/<case>/ to reports/workspace/<case>/judgments/<judgment-id>/, written once, never rewritten. Each judgment retains the exact document it saw.
  • LedgerEntry gains judgment_id. The store rejects a decision citing a judgment the case never reached.
  • Decisions can only be recorded against the judgment in force. The source's stated reason: recording one against a superseded judgment "would be minuting a meeting into the past".
  • analysis.verify_ledger checks that every decision still resolves to artifacts on disk carrying the cited digest. The workspace shows the outcome beside each ledger entry, including a visible failure state. The source states plainly: "There is no quiet failure."
  • An analysis reproducing the current judgment's digest returns that judgment rather than creating a duplicate. The source's stated justification is that the engine is deterministic, so an identical digest means the material reached the same conclusion, and recording it twice would put an event in institutional history that never happened.

Analysis runs in a scratch directory and the finished artifacts are moved into place in one step, so a failed run cannot leave a half-written judgment behind (§ Implementation).

Invariants and their defending tests

The source names seven invariants and the test defending each, in TestSupersession in applications/investment/workspace/tests/test_workspace.py (§ Invariants, and where they are defended):

InvariantTest
Historical decisions remain permanently verifiabletest_a_decision_survives_re_analysis
Historical record digests always resolvetest_every_judgment_ever_reached_keeps_its_artifacts
Re-analysis never invalidates prior decisionstest_decisions_against_different_judgments_all_resolve
Provenance remains completetest_the_material_that_produced_each_judgment_is_kept
Append-only institutional historytest_history_is_append_only
A superseded judgment stays fully readabletest_a_superseded_judgment_still_reads_in_full
Determinism does not manufacture historytest_re_running_unchanged_material_creates_no_new_judgment

Costs the source accepts

The source records three consequences (§ Consequences):

  • Storage grows with every distinct analysis. The source calls this deliberate and cheap — a judgment is roughly 70 KB — and states that retention "is an institutional policy question, not an engineering one, and is not answered here".
  • The case store's on-disk layout changed, and there is no migration path. The source states the reason: the only data in the old layout was generated development data, and records the admission that "A deployed system would have needed one."
  • Case.status() no longer takes an analysed argument, because judgment history lives on the case and status is derived entirely from the case record.

Status of this ruling

The source records its own status as "Approved 2026-08-06. Implemented." (§ header) and repeats "Approved and implemented 2026-08-06" (§ Approval Status). It is an approved and implemented ruling. The source states it is recorded because the ruling "is load-bearing for every future product decision about institutional history" (§ header).

sections.heading: Architectural Implications
sections.html:
The source document does not name CHOIR or DAALE. The constraints below are the ones the source itself draws, stated in its own terms — the case store, the ledger, the judgment record, and the workspace.

Append-only history is a binding constraint, not a preference. The architect's ruling forbids overwriting history and forbids freezing cases (§ Ruling). Any later design that would mutate a judgment record in place, or block re-analysis of a decided case, is ruled out by this decision. The source states the ruling is load-bearing for every future product decision about institutional history (§ header).

Decisions bind to a judgment identity, not to a case. Because LedgerEntry carries judgment_id and the store rejects a decision citing a judgment the case never reached (§ Implementation), any component recording a decision must know which judgment is in force and must record against that one. Decisions can only be recorded against the judgment in force (§ Implementation).

Artifacts are write-once and per-judgment. The move to reports/workspace/<case>/judgments/<judgment-id>/, written once and never rewritten, means each judgment retains the exact document it saw (§ Implementation). Provenance completeness is one of the seven defended invariants (§ Invariants, and where they are defended).

Verification is a first-class, visible operation. analysis.verify_ledger checks that every decision still resolves to artifacts carrying the cited digest, and the workspace surfaces that outcome beside each ledger entry including a visible failure state (§ Implementation). The source's stated commitment — "There is no quiet failure" — makes silent unverifiability unacceptable rather than merely undesirable.

Determinism is relied upon. The de-duplication behaviour — an analysis reproducing the current judgment's digest returns that judgment rather than creating a new one — rests on the stated premise that the engine is deterministic (§ Implementation). That premise is asserted in the source, not demonstrated in it.

Deferral is preserved as an outcome. Freezing was rejected in part because deferral is a first-class outcome in the product and a decided case must remain workable (§ Ruling).

sections.heading: Open Questions
sections.html:
• Retention policy is unanswered. Storage grows with every distinct analysis; the source states that retention "is an institutional policy question, not an engineering one, and is not answered here" (§ Consequences).
  • No migration path exists for the layout change. The source records that none was written because the only data in the old layout was generated development data, and admits that "A deployed system would have needed one" (§ Consequences).
  • Determinism of the engine is asserted, not demonstrated here. The de-duplication rule depends on it, and the source offers no measurement or proof of it within this document (§ Implementation).
